title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook - Comprehensive
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical Redwood Inference on-call and incident response playbook. It defines incident severity, roles and responsibilities, the end-to-end incident lifecycle, runbook templates for common failure classes, postmortem expectations, on-call rotation policy, game day guidance, and customer/status communications templates. Use this playbook during live incidents and as the baseline for runbook and process changes.

Purpose and scope

- Purpose: Reduce time-to-detection, shorten mitigation time, ensure reliable customer communications, and drive post-incident learning and remediation.
- Scope: Applies to all production-facing services owned by engineering teams (runtime, control plane, telemetry, auth, billing). Excludes purely experimental labs environments unless explicitly added to a runbook.

Roles & responsibilities

- Primary on-call (Primary): First responder; owns initial triage and mitigations until incident is escalated.
- Secondary on-call (Backup): Immediate escalation target if Primary needs help or incident is beyond single-person scope.
- Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates cross-team response for Sev1/P0 incidents, owns communications and run of play.
- Service Owner / Pager Owner: Team that owns the affected service; provides technical subject-matter-expertise and implements fixes.
- SRE Lead / Escalation Manager: Responsible for platform-level mitigations (networking, storage, fleet capacity).
- Communications Lead: Drafts status page and customer communications; coordinates with legal/security for sensitive incidents.

Incident severity definitions and target SLAs

- P0 (Production outage, customer-impacting): Service completely unavailable or critical production traffic blocked.
  - Acknowledge target: <= 5 minutes
  - IC declared: within 10 minutes if outage confirmed
  - Restore degraded functionality (initial mitigation): <= 60 minutes (target)
- P1 (Major degradation): Significant latency/errors causing customer impact but partial functionality remains.
  - Acknowledge target: <= 15 minutes
  - Initial mitigation: <= 2 hours
- P2 (Minor impact): Limited feature degradation, elevated error rates with workarounds.
  - Acknowledge target: <= 1 business hour
- P3 (Non-urgent): Low-priority issues, bugs, or improvement requests; handled as standard tickets.

Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)

1. Detection & Alerting
   - Alerts fire via PagerDuty (critical) or Slack automated channels.
   - Primary on-call must verify alert validity within acknowledge target.
2. Triage
   - Determine scope (region, model, tenant), impact (customer-facing, internal), and probable subsystem.
   - Check dashboards: per-route latency, token rates, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, infra alarms.
3. Declaration
   - If impact meets P0/P1, declare incident and assign IC. IC posts incident header in #incidents and opens incident Zoom bridge.
4. Initial mitigation
   - Follow the service-specific runbook. Apply safe mitigations (traffic reroute, scale-up, rollback, increase timeouts).
5. Communication
   - Publish an incident start message to status.redwood.ai and customer comms channel. Use templates below.
   - Update every 30 minutes for P0/P1 until stabilized or resolved.
6. Recovery & Verification
   - Ensure traffic is healthy for 30 continuous minutes and key SLOs are met before declaring resolved.
7. Postmortem & Action items
   - Owner (usually service owner) files a postmortem within 72 hours for P0/P1; within 7 days for P2 if requested.
   - Track action items in the team’s backlog with owners and due dates; follow up in reliability review.

Runbook structure (standard template)

- Title: Service / symptom (e.g., Model-serving: high tail latency)
- Pager condition(s): Alert names and thresholds (e.g., model-serving-inferred-latency-p95 > 500ms for 5m)
- Impact: What customers see and example queries affected
- Detection: Dashboards and logs to check (links)
- Quick mitigations (ordered):
  1. Check cluster capacity: `kubectl get nodes`, GPU utilization dashboards
  2. If heavy queuing: increase replica count by +2 with controlled rollout
  3. If model OOM: revert to previous quantization profile or reduce batch size
  4. If control-plane errors: restart affected control-plane pods one at a time
- Full mitigation steps (detailed commands)
- Escalation path (names and PagerDuty escalation policy)
- Post-incident follow-up checklist

Example runbooks (summaries)

1) Control-plane API 5xx surge
- Symptom: > 10% 500 responses for 5+ minutes across regions.
- Quick checks: API server logs, DB connection pool size, rate limiter metrics.
- Quick mitigations:
  - Apply emergency rate-limit bypass for internal system tokens (if safe).
  - Scale control-plane replicas with gradual rollout.
  - If DB is saturated: switch reads to replica or increase connection pool temporarily.
- Escalation: SRE Lead -> DB owner -> Security if degradation appears malicious.

2) Model-serving latency spike / tokens stalled
- Symptom: p95/p99 token latency spikes, KV cache miss rate increases.
- Quick checks: GPU utilization, queue lengths, cache hit/miss, model variant routing logs.
- Mitigations:
  - Temporarily route traffic to a lower-latency model variant or smaller sequence-length profile.
  - Flush and warm KV cache for hot prefixes if cache corruption suspected.
  - If a recent model rollout coincided, immediate rollback to previous model version.

3) GPU fleet node OOM or repeated container restarts
- Symptom: Node-level OOMs or repeated OOMKilled events in kube events.
- Quick mitigations:
  - Cordon the problematic node, drain gracefully, and reprovision a replacement.
  - Trigger autoscale to add capacity for queued inference jobs.
  - If misconfiguration caused large batch sizes, reduce global batch size via config service.

Postmortem template (required for P0/P1)

- Title
- Incident ID
- Severity
- Start / End time (UTC)
- Summary (brief, customer-facing)
- Impact (customers affected, regions, percent of traffic)
- Timeline (minute-level for first 4 hours, then high-level)
- Root cause analysis
- Contributing factors
- Corrective actions taken during incident
- Remediation and prevention plan (with owners and due dates)
- Detection gaps & monitoring changes required
- Communication timeline (what was communicated, when, where)
- Lessons learned and follow-ups

On-call rotation policy

- Shift length: Primary shift = 7 days (Mon-Sun), Secondary shift = 7 days. Exceptions permitted for minority schedules.
- Handoffs: Handoffs occur at 09:00 PDT on Mondays for week-long rotations. Outgoing on-call must post a handoff summary in #oncall-handoffs.
- Coverage: Each team must maintain a public calendar (Google Calendar) and PagerDuty schedule.
- Escalations: If Primary does not ack within acknowledge window, PagerDuty escalates to Secondary; if Secondary fails to ack, escalate to SRE Lead.
- Long absences: Teams must assign interim coverage and notify eng-sre at least 2 weeks in advance.

Handoff checklist (minimum)

- Current incidents and status updates
- Recent maintenance or rollouts in last 72 hours
- Known flaky alerts and runbooks to watch
- Scheduled game days or maintenance windows this week
- Critical on-call runbook links

Game days (recommended exercises)

- Frequency: Each team runs a minimum of 1 game day per quarter; platform-wide game day semi-annually.
- Objectives: Validate runbooks, test escalations, verify status page workflow, practice cross-team IC coordination.
- Example scenarios: sudden model latency spike, control-plane DB saturation, multi-AZ network partition, bad rollout causing 5xxs.
- After-action: Brief write-up, action list, and follow-up ownership assigned.

Status page & customer comms templates

- Incident start (sitrep):
  Subject: [INCIDENT] Service: <service-name> — <brief impact statement>
  Body: We are investigating reports of <symptom>. Impact: <what customers see>. We will provide updates every 30 minutes. Incident ID: <INC-####>.

- 30-minute update (progress):
  Subject: [UPDATE] <service-name> — <short status>
  Body: Current status: <what changed>. Actions taken: <mitigations>. Next update: <ETA or time>.

- Resolution notice:
  Subject: [RESOLVED] <service-name> — <short resolution summary>
  Body: The incident has been resolved as of <time UTC>. Impact: <who was affected>. Root cause: <summary if available>. Postmortem to follow.

- Postmortem-ready customer summary (public):
  Subject: Incident summary — <service-name> (Date)
  Body: Brief one-paragraph description of impact, cause, and remediation taken, with link to full postmortem once published.

Communication channels and workflow

- Primary incident comms: #incidents (Slack) and the incident Zoom bridge created by PagerDuty every P0/P1 incident.
- Internal escalation: PagerDuty -> #incidents -> @oncall SLO paging.
- Customer comms: Status page (status.redwood.ai) and customer-email list for major incidents. Legal/security must sign off if incident involves data exposure.

Tooling & access

- PagerDuty: alerting and escalation rules; maintain on-call schedule.
- Statuspage (Atlassian): public status updates and incident timeline publishing.
- Grafana / CloudWatch dashboards: latency, errors, capacity, model-specific metrics.
- Runbooks: stored as Confluence pages linked from the runbook index.
- Incident tracker: use internal ticketing (Jira) to track postmortem follow-ups.

Ownership, review cadence, and continuous improvement

- Each on-call runbook must have an owner listed in the runbook header (team and person). Owners review runbooks quarterly or after any incident that exercised the runbook.
- Reliability review: Monthly reliability review meeting to review all P0/P1 postmortems and track remediation progress.
- Metrics: Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to mitigate (MTTM), mean time to restore (MTTR), and number of repeat incidents — tracked monthly by eng-sre. Targets are published on the eng-sre dashboard.

  - Status page editor: https://status.redwood.ai
  - Incident template (Jira): PROJECT-INCIDENT-TEMPLATE
  - Runbook index: confluence://runbooks/index (internal link)

- Contact list (on-call escalation):
  - SRE Lead: Marco Ruiz (pager: +1-555-0101)
  - Platform Ops: Leah Chen (pager: +1-555-0102)

- Version history
  - 2024-10-01: Playbook created (Aisha Patel)

If you are responding to a live incident and this playbook is out of date or missing a critical step, follow the Incident Lifecycle steps and escalate to SRE Lead immediately.
